MCP Server

AI coding assistants are good at writing web components, but they can’t see LoomiUI’s actual attribute names, default values, or events — so they guess. @loomi/mcp-server fixes that by exposing this entire documentation site as an MCP server your AI tool can query directly, the same way you’d ask a teammate “what attributes does <loomi-datepicker> take?”

It ships every component’s docs bundled into the package — no network calls, no access to your filesystem beyond the package itself.

You do not import this package into your app. Your AI editor or assistant starts it in the background when it needs LoomiUI documentation.

What it exposes

Section titled “What it exposes”
ToolWhat it does
list_componentsLists every component, optionally filtered by category (standalone, forms, content, navigation).
search_componentsFinds components by keyword — matches name, description, and category.
get_component_docsReturns the full docs (usage examples, attribute table, events) for one component by name or tag.

Plus a readable resource per component at loomi://docs/<name> (e.g. loomi://docs/button), for clients that prefer direct resource reads over tool calls.

Setup

Section titled “Setup”

Where to put the config

Section titled “Where to put the config”

Choose the tool you use, then add the matching JSON to that tool’s MCP config file. If the file does not exist yet, create it. After saving the file, restart the tool so it can start the loomiui server.

Claude Code

Section titled “Claude Code”

Add the config to your MCP settings. You can use .claude/settings.json in a project, or run /mcp inside an interactive Claude Code session.

Cursor

Section titled “Cursor”

Add this to ~/.cursor/mcp.json for all Cursor projects, or to your project’s .cursor/mcp.json for just one project.

Claude Desktop

Section titled “Claude Desktop”

Add the config to your claude_desktop_config.json file.

Trying it without an editor

Section titled “Trying it without an editor”

Open a regular terminal on your computer, such as Terminal, iTerm, or your editor’s integrated terminal. You can run this from any folder; it does not need to be inside a LoomiUI project or the app where you plan to use LoomiUI.

If it starts successfully, it may look like nothing happened. That is expected. MCP servers communicate over stdio, so this command waits quietly for an MCP client, such as Claude Code or Cursor, to connect.

Press Ctrl+C to stop the test server and return to your terminal prompt.

Using it in your assistant

Section titled “Using it in your assistant”

Once the server is connected, ask your assistant for LoomiUI-specific help:

Your assistant can call get_component_docs for datepicker, see the real range, max-date, and format attributes, and write code against the actual component.

Why this matters

Section titled “Why this matters”

Without the MCP server, an assistant only knows what was in its training data and what you paste into the chat. With the server connected, it can look up the current LoomiUI docs before it writes code.

This mirrors how LoomiUI itself was documented during development — the same list/search/get-docs shape that BladewindUI exposes through its own MCP connector.
